title: On data-driven parameterizations of multidimensional generalized Langevin dynamics in the presence of a quadratic potential
authors: Maximilian Braun, Martin Hanke, Niklas Wolf
abstract: We propose a numerical algorithm to construct a Markov model with an extended list of variables to parameterize the equation of motion of a multidimensional coarse-grained physical system in an external potential, when memory effects are relevant. Our method uses autocorrelation data of the stationary velocities, but it avoids the inverse problem of finding the corresponding memory kernel from these data in a first step. Rather, the data are used to construct a Prony series approximation of the autocorrelation function, and the parameters of this Prony series provide the corresponding Markov model. Numerical results for molecular dynamics data show a good match for parameterized models with five auxiliary variables for a one-dimensional, and twelve auxiliary variables for a two-dimensional system.
summary: This paper presents a novel, data-driven method to convert the description of complex physical systems governed by Generalized Langevin Dynamics (GLEs) into an equivalent, solvable Markovian model. By utilizing autocorrelation functions and Prony series approximations, the authors bypass the difficult step of calculating the memory kernel directly from data. This technique is highly useful for simulating coarse-grained dynamics in condensed matter systems where non-Markovian effects are dominant.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing a numerical algorithm to construct an effective Markov model that parameterizes the equation of motion for complex, multidimensional physical systems exhibiting memory effects.
main_result: The authors successfully show how to bypass the difficult inverse problem by directly using autocorrelation data (via Prony series) to determine the parameters for the equivalent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process.
method: The methodology involves approximating the system's dynamics, governed by a Generalized Langevin Equation (GLE), with an auxiliary variable Markovian model. This is achieved by fitting the velocity autocorrelation function using techniques like the AAA algorithm and Prony series expansion.
model_or_system: The study focuses on coarse-grained physical systems whose motion is described by GLEs in an external potential, often linearized to a quadratic form ($\Phi(x) =  rac{1}{2} x^T \Omega x$). The system dynamics are modeled using auxiliary variables to transform the non-Markovian process into a solvable Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) system.
key_observables: Velocity autocorrelation function ($C_V(t)$), position autocorrelation function ($C_R(t)$), and cross-correlations ($C_{RV}$).
important_parameters: The number of auxiliary variables required for the Markov model (e.g., five for 1D, twelve for 2D) and system parameters like mass ($m$) and potential stiffness ($\Omega$).
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include linearizing the external potential to a quadratic form, assuming the existence of a stationary Gaussian process solution, and approximating continuous autocorrelation data using finite equidistant samples (Markov approximation).
figures_summary: Figures compare the reconstructed position autocorrelation function against known values, showing good agreement for velocity correlations. Error analysis quantifies the performance of the approximations in various correlation functions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework connecting GLEs to OU systems (using system theory concepts) to detailing the data-driven numerical procedure using Prony series and convex optimization solvers, culminating in validation against molecular dynamics simulations.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful computational tool for modeling complex non-Markovian dynamics common in condensed matter physics. The ability to extract effective Markov descriptions directly from measured correlations is highly valuable for simulating systems where memory effects are crucial but analytically intractable.
